name: Shad Khan

views.text: My head coach, general manager and football executive each report to me, not to each other.
If the coach I want needs a different front office, I will change the front office.
A new stadium is part of building a winner here, and I will cover what it takes.
Four seasons without enough progress is enough to start over.
An offensive play-caller who can develop the quarterback is worth chasing hard.
London is part of this franchise's future, not a distraction.

signatures: redraws the org chart when he hires a coach
talks about the stadium and London in the same breath as football

motivation.want: a consistent winner that secures the franchise in Jacksonville
motivation.fear: another coaching reset with nothing to show for it

want.text: a winner to open the renovated stadium

voice: Confident and businesslike, speaks in terms of structure and accountability. Optimistic about the city and the project; brief on football detail.

evidence.summary: Describes the new structure in which head coach Liam Coen, GM James Gladstone and executive Tony Boselli each report directly to Khan.
Khan fired Doug Pederson after four seasons and then GM Trent Baalke, clearing the way to land Tampa Bay OC Liam Coen as head coach.
Owners approved a $1.4 billion EverBank Stadium renovation with the team and city each contributing $625 million and Khan responsible for overruns.
